intro: The forty-ninth screen read 102 pictures, the set's 21 and 81 probes, with thirteen readers and four scorers: 1,095 of 1,114 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **63 of the 64 templates pass the legibility gate, and `square_wheel` does not**: 0.812 in its eight pictures, because two readers of the four wheelbarrows did not notice the wheel and a third named the bicycle's back wheel only among the things it was unsure of. The wheel is the scene's drawing and no line of it changed; the three pictures are the three in which v0.51's readers named the wheel only in passing. Because the set is v0.51's with other figures in it, the screen is also a second reading of v0.51's pictures: 1,054 of the 1,114 items have the score they had, 50 of the 60 others are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out or named, and ten are not, seven of them lower and three higher. Of the 19 items under full marks, twelve are the clouds or a tree; four are the wheelbarrow's, one the bicycle's, one the thief bird's and one the bread's. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. The set's score rose to 0.986, from 0.976. On the strict count 54 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.51's 56. No reader of a whole picture wrote of a sleeve, a shoulder or an arm as drawn, in this screen or the last: the new drawing was judged where it shows, large and in pairs, and chosen there by 10 reviewers of 12, 10 of 12 and 4 of 6. The four grown figures are called young first in 5 of their 85 pictures, as in v0.51.
design:
## Design tests

v0.52 changes the cast and no placement rule, so its test in whole scenes is the bench of `vision/isolation_v052.md` (`vision/design_tests_v052.md`): eighteen of v0.51's screened pictures built again from their own records with the new cast, each with the same templates and the same people as v0.51 drew, and read with the screen's own prompt beside v0.51's own pictures.
- **Who the grown figures are:** called by a young name first in 3 of 35 appearances with the new sleeves, for 4 of 35 in v0.51's pictures read by the same nine readers.
- **Anything new and odd about an arm:** no unsure section has a line on a sleeve, a shoulder or an arm as drawn.
- **The upright sweeper,** read in ten pictures and not taken: grown in all ten, and in all ten with v0.51's pose.

No rule was added after these readings, and no picture was built again for them.
redrawn: Nothing a template draws was changed: every figure has new sleeves and every event is drawn as v0.51 drew it. `square_wheel`, 1.00 in v0.51, reads 0.812 in the same eight pictures and fails the gate, on two wheelbarrows that their readers did not notice. `blocked_hose` and `ice_cream`, 0.95 and 0.967 in v0.51, read 1.00, and nothing was drawn for either: passes their drawings did not earn. `bird_steals` reads 0.944 in six pictures, on one inference not stated, and `ducks_bread` 0.967 in five, on a half mark. `sweep`, whose upright pose was benched and left, reads 1.00 in nineteen pictures. `jump`, `plant_flowers`, `seesaw_heavy`, `play_catch` and `cat_stalks_bird` read 1.00 and are the lowest on the strict count. It is one screen, of 3 to 24 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.17.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (30 in three, 12 in four, 16 in five, 2 in six, and one each in eight, nine, fifteen and nineteen). 63 of 64 pass, where 64 did in v0.51, 62 in v0.50 and 64 in v0.49. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. `square_wheel` is under the gate (0.812 on twenty-four items in eight pictures, no misread). Two more are under 1.00: `bird_steals` (0.944 on eighteen items in six pictures) and `ducks_bread` (0.967 on fifteen items in five); the other 61 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v052/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 34 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 54 of the 64 pass. The failure is not the cast's: the wheelbarrow and the bicycle are the scene's drawing, and v0.51's readers had named the wheel only in passing in the three pictures that failed it. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: Five of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where four had in v0.51, and each by 0.002: `bucket_hat`'s and `sweep_fork`'s two contradiction items and `windy_hat`'s inference. The new sleeves change a figure's outline by a few pixels and no rule, and the planner drew v0.51's set again: all sixteen cells have v0.51's templates on v0.51's seeds. The calibration was measured once, with the cast as it is released.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 48, and every one placed on v0.51's seed with v0.51's templates and v0.51's people in v0.51's places, to within 12 px: tiers 1 to 3 on their showcase seeds, the tier-4 garden on its twenty-sixth step, the street on its twenty-second, the playground on its ninth and the park on the v0.43 seed. The isomorphs are five, two of tier 2, two of tier 3 and one of tier 4, each on v0.51's seed, the last on the third call. The probe pass built 66 and left one template short, the begging dog; three small forced groups filled it, the pass stratified by angle added 9, and three more were forced for the wheelbarrow (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 81 probes, 48 gardens, 21 parks, 10 playgrounds and 2 streets, the same 81 as v0.51's by name and template. **I looked at every picture on sheets before any reader had it, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 102 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 388 of 388. Its soft palette warning is raised by 342 records (340 of 387 in v0.51), with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
